title: Develop The Work And Record A Choice
objective: Develop the pupil’s new collage through a taught trial of contrast and placement, preserving the earlier state and recording an actual creative choice.

blocks.text: Explore · Part C · Create. Develop the work and record a choice.
Today you will look closely at your work, try a change, and choose what to do. Save the work as it is before you move, cover or add a piece.
We are making a new print and collage. A print is a mark pressed from one surface to another. A collage joins pieces to make one image.
Your Part C record needs the making steps and the final artwork. Keep the earlier states even when you prefer the new one. They show how your work grew.
You can point, speak, type or write to show your choices. You may make a pattern or a made-up place. Your art does not have to tell a story about your life.

This deck supports Explore Part C, Create. Part C requires an artwork, a record of the PROCESS, and the final work. The new print-and-collage activity is distinct from the drawing and paper sculpture in Part A and the live or active exploration in Part B. Do not relabel a finished A or B work as C. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. Mark each part P / A / N. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. The whole Explore digital portfolio has a 10-file cap. Organise it by part; four cumulative files, Explore-A, Explore-B, Explore-C and Explore-D, are a suggested arrangement, not one new file per lesson. Every evidence locator must name the actual file plus page, slide or timecode. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Explore; each retains the pupil’s own artwork, process record and final work across C1–C4. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess. Delivery is through a validated centre; staff must confirm these conditions, which this deck does not assert are met. Adults may scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back. They must not write plans, reviews or evidence for the pupil. Staff may record factual observations of access support separately. No visit, booking, meeting or date is asserted. Keep the theme on art choices; no private life account is required.

Explore Part C C3 develops each pupil’s new print-and-collage artwork. Retrieve C1–C2 samples, stage records and the current work. Prepare light and dark dry paper, spare print paper, blunt print tools if further printing is chosen, safe cutting tools and glue sticks. Check access, paint dryness and safe use locally. Model on adult work. Before any pupil alteration, preserve its actual earlier state using a clear image, retained sample or accurate sketch and pupil account. A ring drawn on work that is then covered is not a before-state record. Keep photography optional and credit the photographer. If a pupil’s artwork is missing, retrieve it or arrange further making; do not invent a past stage.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: Place your current collage beside its first sketch or saved image. Find a shape that is still there. Find a step you have made since the start.
What do you notice first when you look at the work? You can point to a print, a paper shape or a space. Look for what catches your eye, not what you think an adult will choose.
Keep the work as it is for a moment. Before you add anything, save a clear record of this state. You will need to look back at it after your next choice.

stages.data-ta1: Give pupils quiet looking time and access to their own record. Check that a real before-state is preserved before any change, including before removing or covering a fixed piece.

stages.title: Starter · create the need

blocks.text: Look at the same grey shape on two scraps. One scrap is pale and one is dark. The shape may stand out more clearly on one of them.
A strong difference between light and dark can help an edge stand out. This is called contrast. You can use it to draw the eye to part of an image.
You may want one clear focus, or you may want the marks to blend. Both can suit an idea. First, look at what is there. Then decide what effect you want.
Would it help to try a loose pale strip beside a dark print before gluing it? Tell a partner what the loose trial would let you check.

stages.data-ta1: Place identical grey shapes against real light and dark papers. Describe the edge difference aloud. Avoid judging one effect as always better; tie choice to the pupil’s intention.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Watch me develop my collage. I want the path of prints to be easy to follow. At this point, one dark print blends into the dark paper beside it.
I save a clear image of the work before I change it. I check that the whole piece is in view. I can still see the dark print and its edge in this record.
I place a pale strip beside the dark print without glue. Its edge now stands out. Then I try a smaller strip. The small strip leaves more of the old paper in view.
I compare the trials with my saved start. I choose the small pale strip because it shows the edge without hiding as much of the print. I fix the strip and keep a new record.

blocks.title: Save a state before a change

boxes.head: SAVE
boxes.line1: keep the work as it is

blocks.caption: The earlier state stays safe when the work changes.
blocks.alt: SAVE: keep the work as it is. TRY: use loose trial pieces. CHOOSE: pick the effect you want. RECORD: show what you did. The earlier state stays safe when the work changes.

blocks.text: My choice is about the effect I want. If a pupil wants a soft edge, their choice may be different. The trial helps them decide for their own image.

stages.data-ta1: Demonstrate an actual before image or sketch, two loose trials and the chosen alteration. Keep the before and after records side by side. Do not model an overwritten ring as preservation.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

data.heading: Find the missing before state
data.instruction: Spot the error in each plan. Choose a way to keep a true making step before it changes.

items.label: “I ringed the edge, then painted over the ring. The ring still records the old layout.”
items.feedback: A separate record remains when the area on the artwork is covered.

options.label: Keep a separate sketch or clear image before painting.
Paint over the rest so nothing can be checked.

items.label: “I will remember it, so no earlier work needs to be kept.”
items.feedback: Memory can help you talk. A kept trial or record lets someone see the making step too.

options.label: Keep a real trial or a clear record of the earlier state.
Write a different story after it is finished.

items.label: “The new strip must be better because it is new.”
items.feedback: A new piece is not automatically the right choice. You can keep the old layout for a reason.

options.label: Compare the actual effect and keep your choice.

data.discussion: Try a light and dark piece beside the same print. Look at the edges. Save your trial before fixing the version you choose.

stages.data-ta1: Take every pupil’s sort response before revealing the key. The cards are printed on the slide. Explain that a sketch and account must accurately show the actual earlier state.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: The before and after records help me name a change. I do not just write that my work got better. I name what I changed and the effect I can see.

blocks.title: A change you can point to
blocks.caption: My words link a real choice to a visible effect.
blocks.alt: BEFORE: dark edge blends in, old state is kept. AFTER: pale strip shows the edge, new state is kept. My words link a real choice to a visible effect.

blocks.text: In my model, I say: I added a small pale strip. Now I can see the dark print edge. These words match the two records.
I might test a change and decide to leave it out. Then I keep the trial and say why I kept the work as it was. Trying and choosing are still part of making.
A helper can record my exact words. They can ask which edge I mean. They should not turn my choice into a new reason that I did not give.

stages.data-ta1: Model a short accurate choice account with the actual evidence visible. A decision to retain the current layout is valid when a genuine material trial and pupil choice are preserved.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: Try a light piece and a dark piece beside the same print on a scrap. Keep both loose while you compare them. Which makes the edge easiest to see?
Now try a wider strip, then a narrow one. Look at how much of the print remains in view. Tell a partner or adult which effect you would choose for this small trial.
Keep a sample or a record of the trial. It gives you a method to use on your main work. You can choose where it fits, or choose a different way to develop the image.

stages.data-ta1: Use spare material for practice so the main work remains intact. Describe the difference for pupils who need visual access support. Preserve the pupil’s response without adding a reason.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Look at the before-state record you just saved. Choose a part of your work to develop. Try a loose piece, a gap or a change of size before you fix anything.
Use what the trial shows you to make your own choice. Add or move a piece if it suits your idea. Then keep the new state and name what you did.

items: Core: use large trial pieces and a helper to steady the work. Choose the effect yourself. Keep the before state, the trial and your own words; keep the final artwork when ready.
Extend: try a change, keep the before and after states, and explain the effect in your own words. Retain the process trail and the final artwork.
Challenge: compare two changes to contrast or space. Choose one or keep the old layout for a reason. Save the trials, the process trail and the final artwork.

blocks.text: Use a note, speech, pointing with labels, or a short recording to show your choice. Make sure the record points to your work and to a step that really happened.

stages.data-ta1: Check the before-state exists before permitting an irreversible alteration. Each route keeps process and final evidence across C1–C4. Scribe exactly and check back; do not write a pupil’s decision.

stages.title: Exit · check the trail

blocks.text: Place the before and after records in order. Can you point to the same area in each? Add your short account of the choice between them.
Save this in the same Explore-C file. Record the actual file name plus page, slide or timecode. Credit any photo. Keep old pages when you add new ones.
Check a join and leave wet work to dry safely. Name a final step for next time. You now have more of the making trail; the finished artwork still needs to join it.

stages.data-ta1: Verify real locators and retained earlier pages. Do not silently replace earlier images with new versions. Record remaining making needs without asserting that the artwork is complete.

print.intro: Develop your new artwork with a real trial. Keep the work as it was, then record what you chose and what happened.
focusRows: My saved work state before I change anything
The light, dark, size or space trial I make
My own choice and the effect I can point to
Actual Explore-C file name plus page, slide or timecode; image credit where used
tiers: Core: use large trial pieces and access help. Keep a before state, your trial, your own words and the final work when ready.
Extend: record a trial, choice and before and after states. Keep the process and final work.
Challenge: compare two changes and explain your choice. Keep both trials, the process and final work.
checks: My before-state record was kept before I changed the work.
I tested an effect with real materials.
My own choice matches a step or trial that happened.
My process trail is kept and will include the final artwork.
I have an actual file name and page, slide or timecode for the record.
